facts.statement: Angolatitan is the first non-avian dinosaur discovered in Angola.
facts.quote: It is also the first non-avian dinosaur discovered in Angola.

facts.statement: The fossil was discovered by Octávio Mateus on May 25 near Iembe in the Bengo province.
facts.quote: The discovery was made by Octávio Mateus on May the 25 near Iembe in the province of Bengo

facts.statement: The genus was formally described by Octávio Mateus and colleagues in 2011.
facts.quote: Angolatitan was described by Octávio Mateus and colleagues in 2011.

facts.statement: The fossilized upper arm bone measures 110 cm and the ulna measures 69 cm in length.
facts.quote: The upper arm bone measures 110 cm, the ulna 69 cm in length.

facts.statement: Unlike other titanosaurs, this dinosaur lacked an olecranon and its first metacarpal was not bowed.
facts.quote: Unlike titanosaurs, the olecranon was absent, and the first metacarpal was not bowed.

facts.statement: Angolatitan was a basal titanosauriform living during the Late Cretaceous, a time when more derived titanosaurs were dominant.
facts.quote: Angolatitan was a relict form of its time; it was a Late Cretaceous basal titanosauriform, when more derived titanosaurs were far more common.

facts.statement: The ecosystem inhabited by Angolatitan was likely desert-like.
facts.quote: The ecosystem inhabited by Angolatitan would have been desert-like.

facts.statement: It lived approximately 90 million years ago during the mid-Cretaceous in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 90 millones de años, en lo que hoy es África.

facts.statement: The animal lived between 89.8 and 85.7 million years ago during the Coniacian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Coniacian to Coniacian (89.8 to 85.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Recent phylogenetic tests classify Angolatitan as a non-titanosaurian titanosauriform.
facts.quote: Recent phylogenetic tests run by Gorsack and Connor (2017) recover Angolatitan as a non-titanosaurian titanosauriform.

facts.statement: The species name 'adamastor' refers to a mythological sea monster representing dangers faced by Portuguese sailors in the southern Atlantic.
facts.quote: The specific name is derived from Adamastor, a mythological sea monster that represented the dangers Portuguese sailors faced in the southern Atlantic.

facts.statement: It is the first named dinosaur from Angola.
facts.quote: es el primer dinosaurio nombrado de Angola.

facts.statement: It is presumed that this sauropod was well adapted to very dry conditions, similar to modern desert elephants.
facts.quote: Presumiblemente, este saurópodo habría estado bien adaptado a las condiciones muy secas, como en el caso con los actuales elefantes del desierto.

rejected.statement: The genus contains only one species, Angolatitan adamastor, known from a partial right forelimb.
rejected.quote: The genus contains a single species, Angolatitan adamastor, known from a partial right forelimb.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'species Angolatitan adamastor known from a partial right'

rejected.statement: It was a large, long-necked herbivorous dinosaur.
rejected.quote: Fueron grandes dinosaurios herbívoros de cuello largo.
